points.text: Steering layer and alpha selected on evaluation data; no validation split, even for universal vector.
Stereotype-reduction claim overstated; holds only vs explicit and mainly English.
Gap measures revealing the answer variable, not latent knowledge; needs abstention and other cues.
Culture-vector specificity untested; no random, non-American or cross-culture controls.
Abstract's conserved universal vector claim stronger than results.
Patching, steering and open-ended results only on Gemma2-9b-it.
No non-cultural control task for patching; universality of mechanisms untested.
Faithfulness claim contradicted by samples naming wrong regions; judge scores within noise.
Judge prompt contains unfilled template slot.
Treatment of GPT-4o refusals in the gap not stated.
'First' claim ignores prior work like Tao et al. and Zhong et al.
'Around 7%' average differs from Table 11's 0.079.
Table 3 and Table 6 disagree on English explicit value.
Title and abstract overclaim; steering recovers only part of the gap.
'Conserved' never defined.
Section 3.3 introduces too many vectors and analyses; hard to follow.
'Explicit' defined inconsistently across figures and tables.
EI-gap equation mixes text probabilities with reported accuracy.
No table reports uncertainty.
Key controls relegated to appendix; caption omits model.
Related work is a list; 'first' claim not argued.
Steering compared only against one prompt template.
Mixed stereotype evidence presented as clear in main text.
Typos, figure order, unexplained colorbar label, removed link.
Language-to-nationality-to-culture assumption under-examined.
Inferring nationality from language is stereotyping; refusals may be correct behavior.
Steering needs white-box access; per-country vectors risk coarse stereotypes.
Qualitative steered samples show thin or wrong cultural targets.
Faithfulness rests on GPT-4o judge with no native-speaker evaluation.
Only five high-resource countries, one low-resource language.
No comparison with fine-tuning or multicultural vector composition.
Pumpkin example a single anecdote.
Vectors and configurations selected and evaluated on same data; no held-out split.
Gap confounds language with context; off-diagonal 2x2 cells unreported.
'Explicit' defined inconsistently across sections.
Model averages include US row where implicit is plain English.
Names/Cities items only answerable with country; headline gaps from synthetic identity items.
GPT-4o generated names, labels and translations unaudited by native speakers.
No CIs on main tables; several claimed differences within noise.
Stated 7% average differs from Table 11's 0.079.
Homogeneity differences tiny; GPT-4o within noise.
Embedding cosine unvalidated as diversity measure; conflates localization with collapse.
Stereotype and faithfulness metrics in Tables 7-8 undefined.
GPT-4o judge lacks human agreement check.
Judge prompt has unfilled template slot.
Patching and steering run on one model only.
No control attribute for patching; layer specificity to culture untested.
Model versions, vector sample counts, injection positions not reported.
Typos, figure numbering, caption omits model.
Table 3 vs Table 6 value mismatch for English explicit.
Text claim about names vector beating task-specific steering contradicts Table 2.
Implicit baseline differs between Table 4 and Table 11.
Homogeneity increase unit ambiguous (absolute vs relative).
Novelty and 'first' claim overstated relative to Tao et al. and Zhong et al.
Prior representation-level cultural steering (CultureSteer, soft prompts) not discussed.
No stronger prompting baselines (persona, few-shot, soft prompt).
Culture vector may be a non-American axis; controls missing.
Abstract's conserved vector claim exceeds partial recovery evidence.
Language treated as culture with one country per language.
Citation mismatches for model reports and order-bias source.
No human evaluation of cultural appropriateness of generations.
Embedding cosine similarity only a proxy for semantic similarity.
Small number of open-ended prompts (24).
GPT embeddings plus GPT judge raises circularity concerns.
Universal steering vector evidence limited; needs robustness, sparsity, side-effect ablations.
Too few low-resource languages.
No cases of different cultures sharing a language.
Culture vaguely operationalized in evaluation datasets.
Three of four benchmarks new and insufficiently validated.
Languages not localized to one culture, e.g., Bengali.
Assumption that language implicitly signals cultural preference is problematic.
One-to-one language-country mapping may be untrue.
Stereotyping not formally defined.
Stereotyping measured only by LLM judge; no human evaluation.
No significance test on Table 1 differences.
Judge prompt lacks option for neither excerpt being stereotypical.
Comparative pairwise stereotype scoring may differ from individual scoring.
EI gap as subtraction of distributions undefined; single-metric computation unclear.
Paper hard to read; Sections 3.2-3.3 unclear, undefined jargon.
Figure 3 formatting inconsistent.
Representational universality claim not validated statistically.
Hard to follow; confusing dataset descriptions and grammatical errors.
Patching and steering procedure insufficiently explained; D+ and D- undefined.
Labels in explicit-implicit gap undefined; Figure 1 uninterpretable.
Cosine similarity not informative of homogeneity; value interpretation unclear.
Reliance on ChatGPT as cultural judge questionable.
Refusal rates uninterpretable without dataset sizes.
Localization-layer claim hard to understand due to unclear methodology.

P.summary: Steering configurations selected on evaluation data.
Gap construct validity: identity-inference items reveal answer.
Culture vector specificity untested; may be non-American axis.
Mechanistic and steering results on a single model.
Faithfulness claim contradicted by qualitative samples.
Unfilled template slot in judge prompt.
'First' novelty claim overstated; related work not differentiated.
Section 3.3 presentation confusing; controls in appendix.
Gap equation mismatched with reported accuracy.
No uncertainty or significance on main results.
Language treated as proxy for single country/culture.
Nationality inference ethics; refusals may be correct.
Deployment risks of white-box per-country vectors.
No native-speaker human evaluation of LLM judge.
Narrow set of cultures and languages.
No comparison with fine-tuning or composition.

Q.summary: No human evaluation; LLM judge reliability questionable.
Cosine similarity a weak proxy for homogeneity.
Universal vector evidence limited; ablations missing.
EI gap definition and labels unclear.
